interest: Early-1930s Japanese salary cuts provoked judicial and railway resistance; salary schedules show the bureaucratic rank system.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.0177) documents efforts and proposals by the Japanese government to reduce civil service and official salaries during the Great Depression between 1930 and 1934. The file includes a subject jacket cover sheet, cross-reference sheets for diplomatic despatches from Tokyo, an excerpt from the May 1931 monthly political report (Despatch No. 240) detailing Prime Minister Reijirō Wakatsuki's salary reduction program across civil service ranks (shinnin, chokunin, sonin, and hannin) alongside opposition from judicial officials and railway workers, and a 1934 U.S. Military Intelligence report transmitting published Diet data on ministerial expenditures for salaries, bonuses, and allowances during the 1931–1932 fiscal year.

subfiles.about: Detailed report extract outlining the Japanese government's graded salary reduction schedule, administrative opposition, and imperial sanction.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: This multi-page extract from Neville's monthly political report (Despatch No. 240) describes the political struggle and policy framework surrounding the Wakatsuki cabinet's civil service retrenchment in May and June 1931, following an earlier abortive attempt under Prime Minister Hamaguchi in 1929. It outlines the preparatory committee's graded salary reduction schedule ranging from 20 percent for the Premier and 12.5 percent for Cabinet ministers down to 3 to 11 percent for lower civil service ranks (shinnin, chokunin, sonin, and hannin), with lower-tier employees exempted. The report also highlights resistance from railway workers and judicial officials claiming statutory protections, the promulgation of Imperial Sanction on May 27 to enforce the cuts, and planned extensions of salary cuts to primary school teachers and Imperial Household Department personnel (with page 8 being a duplicate scan of page 7).
subfiles.title: Despatch Extract on the Wakatsuki Cabinet's Salary Reduction Program
